central_topic: Sensitivity of Bradley-Terry pairwise-comparison leaderboard rankings (rank-1 displacement) to small, evaluator-verified drop/flip edits of comparison data, compared across crowd-vote, expert-human, LLM-judge and sports (NBA) designs; post-draft gaps: poisoning/manipulation positioning, accuracy of first-order group-removal approximations, and sports rating context.
core_methods: Ridge-penalised Bradley-Terry maximum-likelihood fitting of pairwise comparisons
First-order influence-function heuristic with additive per-row effects for choosing drop/flip edits
Exact-refit verification of edited comparison data
comparators: Influence-function-based data poisoning and label-flip attacks on logistic or pairwise models
Adversarial manipulation of rank aggregation and rating systems (Elo/Bradley-Terry)
Group-influence and infinitesimal-jackknife approximations for multi-point removal
benchmarks: NBA regular-season game results (2008, 2012, 2015) as Bradley-Terry/Elo-style sports comparison data
result_driven_themes: Additive first-order approximation may degrade at a 2% edit budget and differ across designs (linearisation-error hypothesis)
Minimal-perturbation sensitivity is a data-poisoning/manipulation question on rankings and needs positioning against that literature
